author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory: veterinarians grouped by specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory listing every specialty by its stored name with the veterinarians who hold it, each by full name (first then last), all on one page with no paging. Veterinarians holding no specialty are omitted.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians who hold it.
A veterinarian holding a specialty appears under that specialty by full name, first name then last name (for example 'Helen Leary').
A veterinarian holding no specialty is not listed; the page indexes specialties and their holders, not the full veterinarian roster.
All specialties appear together on a single page, with no pagination.
A specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, with no veterinarians shown under it.
A veterinarian holding more than one specialty appears under each specialty they hold.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged) — the directory is read-only
notes: Inverse view of REQ-VET-001 over the same veterinarian/specialty association; unlike the veterinarian directory it is not paginated. Product owner specified the public address as /specialties.html, so the design assigns exactly that route. NG-2 confirmed unchanged.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is the inverse projection of the existing veterinarian directory over the same Vet-Specialty ManyToMany association, and lands entirely inside the vet feature package. It reuses three in-force patterns unchanged: Web controller (VetController gains the GET /specialties.html route), Repository (VetRepository gains a cached read method enumerating every Specialty), and server-side Thymeleaf rendering (new templates/vets/specialtyList.html). No new module, type, or dependency. system-design.md Contracts table updated to wire REQ-VET-003 into the Implements column of VetController, VetRepository, Vet, and Specialty. The one adjustment beyond REQ-VET-001's shape is the new repository read method, because the 'specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed' criterion cannot be satisfied by enumerating specialties from the vet roster alone.
integration_points: VetController: add @GetMapping("/specialties.html") -> view name vets/specialtyList; the existing /vets.html and /vets routes are untouched.

VetRepository: add a cached read method returning every Specialty (explicit @Query "SELECT s FROM Specialty s"; the interface is typed Repository<Vet,Integer> but an explicit @Query may return any type). Specialty enumeration is what makes empty specialties appear; deriving specialties from findAll() vets alone silently drops them.

Grouping projection: Specialty has no back-reference to Vet (the ManyToMany is unidirectional from Vet), so the specialty->holders map is built in Java from the full vet list (vetRepository.findAll()) plus the full specialty list. Keep it a private helper on the controller, mirroring addPaginationModel; it is display assembly, not a domain rule.

Template: specialtyList.html renders each specialty by stored name with its holders shown as firstName + ' ' + lastName, reusing the layout fragment and existing #{...} keys (specialties, none) where possible.

patterns.description: existing @GetMapping HTML route + Model + view-name return; the new route is the same shape without pagination
existing @Transactional(readOnly=true) @Cacheable("vets") read method; the specialty enumeration method follows the same annotations
full-name rendering as ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName} — reuse verbatim for the holder rows

risks.risk: REQ-LANG-002 forbids hard-coded user-facing text and partly-translated locales; I18nPropertiesSyncTest asserts all 11 message bundles carry identical keys. Any NEW label key in specialtyList.html must be added to all 11 messages*.properties or the build fails.
risks.mitigation: Prefer the existing keys (#{specialties}, #{none}); if a new heading key is unavoidable, add it to every locale bundle in the same slice. Do not embed literal English in the template.

risks.risk: 'none'/empty-specialty and the multi-specialty (vet under each held specialty) edge cases are easy to miss when grouping.
risks.mitigation: The prd-entry test_names already cover both (shouldListSpecialtyWithNoVeterinarians, shouldShowVeterinarianUnderEachHeldSpecialty); drive them TDD-first against the H2 seed data.

risks.risk: Vet ordering within a specialty is unspecified by the acceptance criteria, which makes MockMvc assertions on rendered order brittle.
risks.mitigation: Sort holders deterministically (e.g. by last name then first name) so tests are stable; the order itself is not requirement-bearing.

notes: Verdict minor (not covered) because of the small system-design.md Implements-column update and the new VetRepository read method — a thin extension point on an existing pattern, no new pattern or type. NG-2 (no management of vets/specialties) stays intact: the directory is read-only. Checklist: no new business rule enters the controller (grouping is presentation projection, so it does not extend the recorded Web-controller deviation); no new dependency; placement stays within the vet package with no cross-module reach; the read path is unauthenticated like every other route, consistent with the confirmed demonstration security posture (no new trust boundary introduced). If the implementer judges an explicit @Query returning Specialty from a Repository<Vet,Integer> to be the wrong home, raise a consultation before adding a separate SpecialtyRepository — the prd-entry file_targets name VetRepository, and PetTypeRepository is the only lookup-value repository precedent. No design-doc-autofix records since first slice; autofix audit is a no-op.

findings.description: The CacheConfiguration row description ends with 'Each no-arg read holds its own named cache so their results never share a key'. The clause 'so their results never share a key' is rationale prose explaining the purpose of the two-cache design — a 'why' explanation prohibited in system-design.md. Rationale belongs in an ADR with a back-link; the design doc carries only the rule. The phrase 'no-arg read' additionally ties the description to the current zero-argument method signatures and silently fails the self-test: if either findAll() or findSpecialties() gains a parameter, this phrase becomes wrong without any source change touching this row. Class sweep of the other changed rows found no further 'why' clauses.

Two inline 'because' clauses introduce rationale into the PRD. Line 137 narrative: 'Because it indexes specialties rather than people, a veterinarian who holds no specialty appears under none'. Line 142 Done-when bullet: 'then that veterinarian is not listed, because the directory indexes specialties and their holders rather than the full veterinarian roster'. The PRD boundary rule prohibits 'why' content; rationale belongs in an ADR. The prohibited-pattern table lists 'paragraphs explaining why' as Critical — these are single-sentence clauses, making severity borderline. The Done-when bullet at line 142 runs to 32 words (above the 30-word limit), with the excess being the 'because' clause. Question for product-requirements-expert: does the 'because' clause qualify as scope-defining behavioral description that can remain, or as decision rationale that should move to an ADR with a back-link?

The sentence 'A specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, and under each the veterinarians who hold it, each shown by full name — first name then last name, such as "Helen Leary".' runs to 35 words, exceeding the 30-word sentence limit. The example 'Helen Leary' is preserved in the Done-when bullet at line 141.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Additive read-only feature: one new GET route, one new cached @Query read, a second named cache alongside the existing one, plus a new template. Three modules but all within the vet feature and one cache-config bean; no sensitive paths, no modification of existing behavior.

semantic_surprise.note: Grouping logic reads exactly as the inverse-directory description implies: specialties enumerated independently and sorted, holders filtered by name-match and sorted by last-then-first name, empty specialties preserved via LinkedHashMap. The separate specialties cache correctly avoids the SimpleKey.EMPTY collision the ADR documents. No inverted operators or hidden behavior.

test_adequacy.note: Six MockMvc tests assert real outcomes over the changed behavior and every stated edge case: empty specialty (dentistry maps to empty), multi-specialty vet (Rafael under both), omission of specialty-less vet (Carter absent), and no-pagination. Repository mocking is the sanctioned MockMvc controller-test boundary; the grouping under test is real.

reviewer_hedging.note: Full four-reviewer battery all approved with empty findings lists. Round-1 autofix items (test naming, redundant comment, weak assertions) were applied and round 2 approved clean. No escalate, no bar_clause, no lingering caveats.

scope_deviation.note: design_revisions=3 (the design evolved toward the two-cache approach, captured in a new ADR) but build_retries and consultations are zero and the final diff sits squarely on REQ-VET-003 stated surface: unpaged inverse directory, empty specialties listed, multi-specialty vets under each. No wandering past the requirement.

rationale: Additive read-only inverse-directory view; grouping logic matches the spec, the separate named cache correctly dodges the no-arg key collision the ADR documents, and six tests cover every stated edge case. Full roster approved clean. Confirm and merge with a quick read.
